deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The next page is headed 'Erste Beobachtungen mit Repsolds Kreise', 1818 April 20-23, Göttingen. This page reduces catalogue mean declinations of fundamental stars to apparent places for the observation dates. Those places are compared with the Repsold meridian-circle readings to fix the equator point of the circle. The page also reduces the Vesta observation of April 20. Angles in the auxiliary columns are written as degrees.minutes, e.g. 303.56 = 303°56'.

GENERAL SCHEME (my notation). Apparent declination is

delta_app = delta_0 + mu_delta * t + A_ab * sin(Sun + B_ab) + A_nut * sin(Omega + B_nut) + A_s * sin(2*Sun + B_s).

- delta_0 is the catalogue mean place and mu_delta the annual precession (with proper motion).
- Sun is the Sun's longitude and Omega the longitude of the Moon's node.
- The first term is annual aberration in declination, -k[cos(Sun) cos(eps)(tan(eps) cos(delta) - sin(alpha) sin(delta)) + sin(Sun) cos(alpha) sin(delta)], folded into one sinusoid.
- The second is the principal lunar nutation, Delta_psi*sin(eps)*cos(alpha) + Delta_eps*sin(alpha), folded into one sinusoid.
- The third is the small solar semi-annual nutation.
- Each column holds: the star constant B; the date argument (Sun, Omega, 2*Sun); log A; and log sin(argument), with 'n' marking a negative value. The products are the corrections in the left column.

REGULUS (April 20).
- Mean place 12°52'2.6" at epoch 1815.0. The annual precession in delta is 17.32" (=20.05 cos alpha, negative). Then 17.32 x 3.30 yr = 57.16", subtracted.
- Aberration: B=303°56', Sun=30°05', sum 334°01'. log sin = 9.6416n and log A = 0.8429 (A=6.965"), giving -3.05".
- Nutation: B=38°10', Omega=39°18', sum 77°28'. log sin = 9.9895 and log A = 0.8968, giving +7.70".
- Solar term: B=33°, 2*Sun=60°, sum 93°. log sin = 9.999 and log A = 9.664, giving +0.46".
- Sum (mine): 12°52'2.6" - 57.16 - 3.05 + 7.70 + 0.46 = 12°51'10.55". The next page has 12°51'10.6".
- From B and A one recovers the constants used: aberration k = 20.25" and nutation Delta_eps amplitude about 9.65" (ratio 9.65/7.18 = 1.345).

SIRIUS (south; magnitudes of |delta|).
- Mean place 16°28'14.40". The annual change 4.38" (precession plus proper motion), x 3.30 = 14.45".
- Aberration: 85°54' + 30°05' = 115°59'. 1.1129 + 9.9537 gives +11.66".
- Nutation: 263°4' + 39°18' = 302°22'. 0.9819 + 9.9267n gives -8.10".
- Solar term: 262 + 60 = 322°. 9.690 + 9.789n gives -0.30".
- Sum (mine): 16°28'32.11", i.e. delta = -16°28'32.1" as on the next page.

ALPHA CYGNI (observed 'April 22', presumably civil morning, i.e. astronomical April 21 about 18h).
- Mean place 44°37'27.70". The cancelled 45°22'32.30" is the co-declination 90°-delta, first written and then struck out.
- Annual change 12.57", x 3.3055 = 41.55".
- Aberration: 240°44' + 31°32' (Sun) = 272°16'. 1.2610 + 9.9997n gives -18.23".
- Nutation: 239°5' + 39°13' (Omega moved -5', i.e. about 1.6 days) = 278°18'. 0.9426 + 9.9954n gives -8.67".
- Solar term: 234 + 63 = 297°. 9.677 + 9.950n gives -0.42".
- Sum (mine, not written on the page): 44°37'41.93". This is exactly the value on the next page.

VESTA (April 20).
- Declination: the next page's circle reading 46°19'37.2" plus refraction 61.1" gives 46°20'38.2" (my inference).
- The equator point is 51°40'55.5". I checked it: Regulus 38°48'57.7" + 46.7" + 12°51'10.6" = 51°40'55.0", and Sirius 68°7'8.0" + 142.4" - 16°28'32.1" = 51°40'58.3".
- D = 51°40'55.5" - 46°20'38.2" = +5°20'17.3".
- Right ascension: transit clock time 13h19m14.87s, then corrections.
  - -0.28s: clock rate +1.00s/day over the 6.7h since the 6h37 clock check.
  - -1.28s: constant term of the instrumental formula 'Correction = -1.28 + 2.90 tan delta - 3.41 sec delta' (next page).
  - +0.03s: should be the tan-delta term.
  - -3.42s: = -3.41 sec(5°20').
  - Result: alpha = 13h19m9.92s = 199°47'28.8".
- Mean time of meridian passage:
  - The clock was 2.37s slow at 6h37 and gains 1s/day, so it was 2.09s slow at 13h19. Hence sidereal time is 13h19m14.87s + 2.09s = 13h19m16.96s.
  - Subtract the sidereal time at mean noon, 1h51m45.95s, giving 11h27m31.01s sidereal interval.
  - Convert sidereal to mean time: -11.4586 h x 9.8296 s/h = -1m52.63s.
  - Result (mine): 11h25m38.38s, written 'M Zeit 11h25'38"4'.

POLLUX (about April 25/26).
- Mean place 28°29'46.80" at epoch 1800.0 (Piazzi-type catalogue).
- Annual precession 8.08". Then 8.08 x 18 = 145.44 and 8.08 x 0.316 = 2.55, total 147.99" = 2'27.99", subtracted. This gives 28°27'18.81".
- Aberration: 14°57' + 35°49' (Sun) = 50°46'. 0.6009 + 9.8886 gives +3.09".
- Nutation: 72°1' + 38°59' (Omega) = 111°0'. 0.9684 + 9.9790 gives +8.86".
- Solar term: 68 + 71°38' (2*Sun) = 139°38'. 9.685 + 9.811 gives +0.31".
- Total: 28°27'31.07".

PURPOSE. These apparent places (and the Vesta reduction) feed the table on the next page. That table gives the equator point, refraction, and the clock and instrument corrections of Gauss's new Repsold meridian circle.
errors: Pollux nutation: 72°1' + 38°59' = 111°0', and log sin 111° = 9.9702, not 9.9790 as written. With the correct log the correction is +8.68" rather than +8.86" (possibly a digit transposition), so the apparent declination should be about 28°27'30.89" instead of 31.07". Unless the star constant was misread, this is a slip of 0.18".
Pollux aberration: log sin(50°46') = 9.8890, not 9.8886. This is negligible; the product still rounds to +3.09".

Vesta RA: with the next page's formula, 2.90 tan(5°20') = +0.27s, but the page uses +0.03s. With +0.27 the RA would be 13h19m10.16s rather than 9.92s. Either the coefficients differed when this was computed (the formula on the next page may postdate it) or this is a slip; the arithmetic sum itself (9.92) is correct.

The Sun's-longitude arguments (30°05' for April 20, 31°32' for the α Cygni date) differ by only about 1.5 days of solar motion. This agrees with the change in Omega (-5') and in 2*Sun (60 to 63), so it is internally consistent: α Cygni was probably observed in the civil morning of April 22 (astronomical April 21). Not an error, but the dating needs care.
All other sums and logarithm products check: Regulus 10.55", Sirius 32.11", α Cygni 41.93", Pollux sum, D = 5°20'17.3", RA in arc 199°47'28.8", mean time 11h25m38.38s.

results.what: Reduction of catalogue mean declinations to apparent declinations: precession (with proper motion), annual aberration (k = 20.25"), lunar nutation (amplitude about 9.65") and solar semi-annual nutation, each written as a single sinusoid A sin(argument + B) and evaluated by logarithms.
results.modern_name: Reduction from mean to apparent place (precursor of Bessel day numbers / star constants)
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley (aberration, nutation), Lalande/Delambre/Zach tables; Bessel's systematic star constants (Tabulae Regiomontanae, 1830)

results.what: Declination of Vesta from meridian-circle reading plus refraction, referred to an equator point found from fundamental stars of known apparent declination.
results.usually_credited_to: standard practice of meridian astronomy (Bessel, Gauss, et al.)

results.what: Right ascension of Vesta from transit time with clock rate and a Mayer-type instrumental correction a + b tan(delta) + c sec(delta).
Conversion of a sidereal clock time to local mean time via sidereal time at mean noon and the sidereal-to-mean factor 9.8296 s/h.
results.modern_name: Sidereal to mean solar time conversion

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine observatory reductions of apparent places and a meridian observation of Vesta, made during the first trials of Gauss's Repsold meridian circle in April 1818. Gauss's meridian-circle work at Göttingen is well documented; nothing here is mathematically or historically unexpected.

checkable.asserts: Regulus aberration term about 3.05" (negative sign since sin<0)
tan-delta term is about 0.27s, not 0.03s as used for Vesta
Pollux nutation term about 8.68", versus 8.86" written

transcription_corrections: Epoch at top of Regulus: probably '1815...' rather than '1818': the precession intervals (57.16/17.32 = 3.30 yr, 14.45/4.38 = 3.30) imply mean places for 1815.0 reduced to 1818 April.
Cancelled line under α Cygni '45.22.32.30' is the co-declination 90°-44°37'27.70"; the final α Cygni sum (44°37'41.93") is not written, only a rule is drawn.
'Gegd.' next to -0,28 is probably 'Gang' (clock rate correction).
In the Zeit column the sidereal time at noon reads 1.51.45,95 (overwritten digits); the result is 11.27.31,01 and the conversion is -1.52,63.
Pollux scratch line: '8.08 18' = annual precession 8.08" x 18 years = 145.44, plus 2.55 for the fraction of 1818 (total 147.99" = 2'27.99"); the small fraction next to it is uncertain.
Auxiliary column entries such as 303.56, 263.4, 39.18, 30.5, 71.38 are degrees.minutes (303°56', 263°4', 39°18', 30°5', 71°38').
